headline: product-catalog is intermittently rejecting GetProduct calls (its own span cites a 'Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag'), cascading HTTP 500s into cart, recommendations, product pages, and checkout via frontend. Sustained heavy failure 07:56-08:20 UTC, now tapering in ~5-10 min bursts, most recent burst 08:50 UTC, quiet since.
blast_radius: During active bursts: ~47% of checkout attempts fail (144 failed / 162 ok observed), ~38-47% of product detail page loads fail across all 10 catalog product IDs, and recommendations calls fail at a comparable rate. Cart, product browsing, and purchasing are all degraded because every one of those routes calls product-catalog's GetProduct to hydrate data. Unrelated routes not depending on product-catalog (e.g. /api/data?contextKeys=accessories, ~1.8% failure) are unaffected, so the blast radius is bounded to this one dependency's callers, not system-wide.
reasoning: Single alert, single root cause, so DECLARE rather than ATTACH/MERGE (nothing else is open) or SPLIT (there's only one causal thread here, not two). Chose sev2 over sev1 because the failure is intermittent and self-recovering between bursts rather than a total, unrecovering outage, but it directly hits the revenue-critical checkout path at a high rate during bursts, which rules out sev3/sev4. Status is 'open' rather than 'monitoring' or 'resolved': the most recent burst (08:50 UTC) is only ~7 minutes old at time of writing, and every prior quiet gap of similar length (e.g. 08:23-08:29, 08:41-08:47) was followed by another burst, so a ~7-minute quiet window is not yet evidence of recovery -- it matches the established intermittent pattern, not a break from it.

revisions.change: Independent re-review completed. Proposal approved on the merits (all four checks re-derived from primary sources), but not merged: no PR exists for it and a repository merge cannot apply a live flagd config change. Incident stays open.

rca.root_cause: product-catalog's GetProduct gRPC handler is gated by checkProductFailure, which evaluates the OpenFeature/flagd boolean flag productCatalogFailure (default false, generated binding flags.ProductCatalogFailure) per-request via a targetless evaluation context keyed on product_id. When the flag evaluates true for a given request, GetProduct returns before ever calling getProductFromDB, setting a gRPC error with code Internal (13) and the literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled' -- exactly matching the trace evidence (rpc.grpc.status_code=13, grpc.error_message text) verbatim. Because nearly every user-facing route (product detail, cart, recommendations, checkout) calls GetProduct to hydrate product data, this single upstream fault cascades into HTTP 500s across all of them, which is exactly the blast radius alert-grouping observed. This is the demo's deliberate fault-injection code path executing correctly as designed when the flag is on for a given evaluation, not an accidental bug in the flag-check logic itself -- the bursty on/off pattern reflects the flag being toggled/cycled by the fault scenario, not a malfunction in checkProductFailure.
rca.verify_detail: A second, fresh sub-agent, given only the bare claim (file src/product-catalog/main.go, function checkProductFailure, called from GetProduct, gRPC code Internal, literal message 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', returned before the DB lookup) and no prior reasoning, independently confirmed via `gh api repos/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/contents/src/product-catalog` that the file exists at that path, then fetched the real raw content and quoted: GetProduct calling checkProductFailure at line 373; checkProductFailure at lines 419-420 evaluating flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value(ctx, openfeature.NewTargetlessEvaluationContext(map[string]any{"product_id": id})); and the error branch at lines 374-377 returning status.Error(codes.Internal, msg) with msg == 'Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled', with getProductFromDB only reached afterward at line 380. Verdict: CONFIRMED -- every specific element of the claim (path, function, caller, flag reference, error code, exact message, ordering relative to the DB call) is directly and verbatim supported by the real file content, not a plausible-sounding guess.

remediation.pr_error: Branch committed but push blocked by this environment's command guard ("Destructive command detected - confirm before running") on `git push`. The guard needs interactive confirmation and this capability runs unattended, so there was nobody to give it; I did not override it, because pushing to a shared repo is outward-facing and silently disabling a safety check to do it unattended is not mine to decide. Not an auth problem - gh is authenticated and viewerPermission on satya-brata645/trata-sreoncall is WRITE, so no fork is needed. Commit 02f4299b8d84caefa352a4766a82306c7419dcb6 on branch remediation/inc-001-product-catalog-1786278957 is ready in the throwaway clone /private/tmp/sreoncall-pr-inc-001-1786278957, PR body written to /private/tmp/pr-body.md. Exact commands to finish are in sre-engineer/remediations/inc-001/PR-PENDING.md. The proposal itself is complete and reviewed; only transport failed.
remediation.second_opinion: VERDICT: CLEAN - "the defect I flagged is fully closed. The precedence model matches flagd's documented behavior, the Case B remedy is correct and robust to defaultVariant, Step 1 genuinely separates the cases, the live /status reading corroborates the Case B prediction, and the failure mode of every remaining gap is 'operator stalls,' never 'operator causes harm.' The two recommendations above make it more robust; neither is a reason to withhold it." | The same reviewer FLAGGED the first draft: "The committed targeting block returns 'off' in both branches and would take precedence over defaultVariant in flagd, so the live manifest must have diverged in targeting, which the proposed /toggle/<flag>/off (a defaultVariant selector) cannot reach - the fix may silently no-op, and the proposal's claim that it 'restores the committed definition' is not supportable without a pre/post read of /status/productCatalogFailure." That flag was correct and was fixed in the one allowed revision.
remediation.summary: No code change needed anywhere: product-catalog's flag-check code has no defect and the committed upstream flagd config is already 'off' in every branch, so this is runtime drift - proposed a read-first, two-case procedure to make productCatalogFailure evaluate false on the live flagd, which this capability may not apply itself.
not_addressed: Frontend cascade resilience: one non-essential dependency's Internal error becomes user-visible HTTP 500s on cart, product detail, recommendations and ~47% of checkouts. Arguably the more consequential reliability defect, but rca verified src/product-catalog/main.go only - no frontend file was verified or read, so proposing a patch there would rest on code I have not read. Belongs in the postmortem as a recommendation and in a future shift as its own investigation.

Live flag state could not be read: the flagd control API at 10.10.1.141:4001 exposes only static manifest fields (/status, /list return defaultVariant + description, no targeting), and has no read-only evaluation route (POST /ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags/productCatalogFailure -> 'unknown route'). Its only live-state route is /toggle, which this capability may never call. So 'the flag is currently on' is an inference from trace evidence, not a reading.

four_checks.1_reindependently_refetched_implicated_s: PASS. I did not trust remediation's or rca's copy. Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/main/src/product-catalog/main.go myself (12404 bytes) and read the real bytes: GetProduct calls `if p.checkProductFailure(ctx, req.Id) {`, then `msg := "Error: Product Catalog Fail Feature Flag Enabled"`, `span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, msg)`, `return nil, status.Error(codes.Internal, msg)` -- and only past that branch `found, err := getProductFromDB(ctx, req.Id)`. checkProductFailure is a one-liner returning flags.ProductCatalogFailure.Value(ctx, openfeature.NewTargetlessEvaluationContext(map[string]any{"product_id": id})). Every element of the verified RCA reproduces verbatim against source I pulled independently. The other GetProduct failure mode returns codes.NotFound, not Internal, so the trace evidence (code 13) can only have come from the flag branch. RCA confirmed on my own reading.
four_checks.2_minimal_and_scoped_to_verified_cause: PASS. Inspected the actual commit 02f4299b8d84caefa352a4766a82306c7419dcb6 in the preserved clone /private/tmp/sreoncall-pr-inc-001-1786278957: `git diff --name-status main...HEAD` shows exactly two additions -- sre-engineer/remediations/inc-001/proposed-change.md and rationale.md, 464 insertions, 0 deletions, no source file touched anywhere. Zero lines of product code, config, or CI are modified. I also independently re-fetched src/flagd/demo.flagd.json from upstream main and confirmed the proposal's load-bearing claim myself: the committed productCatalogFailure.targeting is `{"if":[{"==":[{"var":"product_id"},"OLJCESPC7Z"]},"off","off"]}` -- both branches "off", defaultVariant "off", variants {off:false,on:true}, state ENABLED. So the committed config genuinely cannot produce this incident and no repo change is warranted; declining to patch main.go is the correct scoping, not an omission.
four_checks.3_no_reckless_pattern: PASS, and deliberately so on several axes I checked for. Nothing is swallowed: there is no code, and the proposal does not suggest catching or suppressing the Internal error rather than removing its cause. No safety check is removed: Step 2 explicitly keeps `state: ENABLED` and both variants defined in every case -- it selects a variant value rather than deleting the fault-injection mechanism, so the ability to run this scenario deliberately later survives. Nothing that should stay configurable is hardcoded: the only hardcoded literal is the Case B targeting block, and I diffed it programmatically against the real committed object -- it is semantically identical, so it restores rather than invents. Detectability is improved, not degraded: it adds a 15-minute flat-zero verification window justified against this incident's own observed 6-10 minute quiet gaps, adds all-10-product-IDs success as the specific signature of a surviving targeting rule, and explicitly forbids rollback (re-enabling the flag) as a response to failed verification. The 'neither case matches -> stop, do not apply either remedy' branch is the opposite of forcing a change through.
four_checks.4_syntactically_valid: PASS. All three fenced json blocks in proposed-change.md parse under json.loads; the Case B object parses and compares equal to the real upstream committed object. No Go was written, so there is nothing to compile.

release_approval.own_re_review: I reached my own verdict from the artifact, not from remediation's rationale (which I did not read) and not from its second opinion. All four checks PASS -- the proposal is technically sound, evidence-grounded, correctly scoped, and I re-derived its central factual claims from primary sources myself rather than inheriting them. I also took my own live reading of the flagd control API: GET http://10.10.1.141:4001/status/productCatalogFailure returns {"ok":true,"flag":"productCatalogFailure","defaultVariant":"off",...}, which independently reproduces the proposal's Step 0 result and confirms Case A's precondition is not met, so Case B is the expected shape -- the same conclusion the all-10-product-IDs blast radius predicts. I could NOT independently verify the claim that flagd exposes no read-only evaluation route: my POST probe to /ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags/productCatalogFailure was declined by this environment's command guard, so that one claim rests on remediation's report rather than my own reading, and I am recording that rather than implying I checked it. Separately, on my own analysis: I compared live behaviour against upstream `main`, not against whatever revision is actually deployed, so 'runtime drift' could in principle be version skew instead. It does not change the remedy (restore-to-committed yields off either way) and it does not rescue the committed config, because even an older revision scoped to the single product OLJCESPC7Z could not produce failures across all 10 catalog product IDs. The divergence conclusion holds on my own reasoning. Despite all four checks passing, I did not merge, for a reason that is not a defect in the proposal -- see objection.
release_approval.objection: There is nothing to merge, and merging would not remediate anything even if there were. Two distinct facts, both verified: (1) No PR exists. remediation's push of branch remediation/inc-001-product-catalog-1786278957 was blocked by this environment's command guard and it correctly declined to override it; `gh pr list --state open` on satya-brata645/trata-sreoncall returns only #9 (a human's postmortem branch), #4 (the earlier agent-prototype), and #3 -- none of them this run's proposal. `gh pr merge` has no target and I will not manufacture one, because pushing the branch myself would make me the author of the delivery I am supposed to be independently checking, which destroys the exact separation this skill exists to provide. (2) Even a merged PR would not close inc-001. The change is a runtime configuration edit to the live flagd instance; no repository merge applies it, and this capability may never call /toggle. The proposal is honest about this -- its terminal step is addressed to an actor with authority over the fault-injection state, and there is no such actor inside this loop. So the correct outcome is: the proposal stands as reviewed and approved on the merits, the incident stays OPEN, and the unblocked action is transport (push + `gh pr create` per PR-PENDING.md) plus an operator with fault-injection authority running Step 0/1/2 -- not a merge by me.
release_approval.merits_verdict: APPROVED ON MERITS -- all four checks pass. Withheld only for absence of a PR and absence of merge as an effective delivery mechanism. If the branch is pushed and a PR opened unchanged, this review stands and it is mergeable as a documentation-only change.

also_reviewed_not_approved.why_considered: It is open, unmerged, and proposes a fix for this same fault (product-catalog feature flag), so I reviewed it on the merits rather than dismissing it because its incident label is INC-0001 from the earlier agent-prototype lineage rather than inc-001 from this shift. Ignoring a still-open fix for the same fault on a naming technicality would be a rule, not a judgment.
also_reviewed_not_approved.objection: Two specific defects, not a vague risk. First, its runbook hardcodes `Current Status: Enabled` as a permanent statement of live flag state. That was never verifiable from the control API, and my own live GET /status just now returns defaultVariant "off" -- so the repo would carry a stale state claim that a future responder is invited to trust instead of reading. Second, its entire Resolution Step 2 is 'disable the fail feature flag', which is exactly the single-action remedy that is provably capable of silently no-opping here: the committed targeting block returns "off" on both branches and takes precedence over defaultVariant, so the live divergence must be in targeting, and a variant selector cannot reach a targeting block. A runbook that sends the next responder to an ineffective action and then to 'monitor error rates' would make the next occurrence of this incident harder to diagnose, not easier. That is the reckless-pattern check failing, so it does not merge on my word.
